title: AssetCore UAT
headline: Work through it, mark what breaks
tagline: Round 3: the surface two rounds never reached — QR labels, the scan page, stock movement, report files, and the cross-cutting checks nobody has run.
intro: Rounds 1 and 2 closed 14 defects but left 17 of round 1's original untested cases still untested, and re-clicked only some of round 1's JavaScript-driven passes. This round goes after exactly that: the parts of the app that have never been watched working. It also re-checks the round-2 fixes that a later change could plausibly have broken. Run against a local stack — API on 8787, app on 5174, database assetcore_integrate — not staging.
url_hint: The app runs at http://localhost:5174 and the API at http://localhost:8787. Ask Claude Code to start them both if the link is dead.

sections.title: Labels, scanning and the field loop
sections.blurb: The technician's path: print a label, scan it, find the asset. Round 1 listed this as r1t48 and never ran it.

tests.title: Print a sheet of QR labels from the asset list
tests.intro: The codebase carries components/AssetQr.jsx — a QR code and a printable label sheet with its own print stylesheet. This test asks whether a user can reach it.
steps: Assets → select two or three assets.
Look for a Labels, QR or Print action on the list or in the row menu.
Open it and check the sheet previews one label per asset.
tests.expect: A label sheet opens showing one QR per selected asset with its AIN beneath, and Print produces the same sheet.

tests.title: Scan page: look up a real tag by hand
tests.intro: The scan page takes a camera feed or a typed tag. The camera cannot be driven here; the manual path can, and it is the same lookup.
steps: Open /scan.
Type NGML-MTR-0042 into the manual field and submit.
Read the asset card that comes back.
tests.expect: The Lagos DS-04 Metering Station card appears with its status, criticality and commissioned date — the date filled in, not blank (round 2 fixed the column name behind it).

tests.title: Scan page: an unknown tag is refused in a sentence
tests.intro: A label from another site, or a smudged read. The page must say so rather than showing a code or an empty card.
steps: On /scan, enter NGML-NOPE-9999.
Read the message.
tests.expect: A sentence naming the tag — no raw not_found, no blank card.

tests.title: A scan URL opens the asset directly
tests.intro: A printed label encodes /scan?ain=… so a phone camera opens the asset. That query parameter path has never been exercised.
steps: Navigate to http://localhost:5174/scan?ain=NGML-VLV-0089 directly.
Check the asset resolves without typing anything.
tests.expect: The Warri T-A Isolation Valve card renders from the URL alone.

sections.title: Stock actually moves
sections.blurb: Round 2 proved a part could be reserved on a job. Nobody has yet watched stock fall when the job closes — r1t37's other half.

tests.title: Closing a work order draws its reserved parts out of stock
tests.intro: consumeParts() in workOrders.ts runs on the transition to closed: it decrements quantity_in_stock, writes a stock movement and stamps consumed_at. Round 2 left WO-2025-0041 holding one reserved SP-PT-1100 against a stock of 2.
steps: Note the on-hand figure for SP-PT-1100 on Spare Parts.
Open WO-2025-0041 and close it.
Return to Spare Parts and read the on-hand figure again.
Open the part and look for the issue in its movement history.
tests.expect: On-hand falls from 2 to 1, the work order's part line reads as consumed rather than reserved, and a movement row records the issue against the job.

tests.title: A job cannot be closed against stock that isn't there
tests.intro: insufficient_stock (409) with a shortfall list is one of the app's own stated rules. Reserving more than exists and closing is the only way to reach it.
steps: On an open work order, reserve SP-PT-1100 with a quantity above what is on hand (say 50).
Try to close the job.
tests.expect: The close is refused in a readable sentence naming the shortfall — not a raw insufficient_stock, and the stock figure does not go negative.

sections.title: Reports produce a file
sections.blurb: r1t43: generate a report and check the file against what the screen says. Never run, and the generator was rewritten from a stub.

tests.title: Request and generate a report, then compare it to the screen
tests.intro: POST /reports/:id/generate builds a real XLSX or CSV synchronously and records a byte size. The check that matters is whether the file's row count agrees with the list it claims to report.
steps: Reports → request an asset register as CSV.
Generate it and wait for Ready.
Note the row count implied by the Assets page (6 assets).
Download the file and open it.
tests.expect: Status goes pending → ready with a non-zero size, and the file holds a header row plus one row per asset, matching the Assets list.

tests.title: A report the Viewer must not be able to request
tests.intro: Round 2 gated GET /reports on report:read and left the Viewer holding it through *:read. report:create is a different capability — the Viewer should be able to read the page and not to generate.
steps: As the Viewer open /reports.
Look for a request/generate control, and try it if it is offered.
tests.expect: Either no create control is offered, or using it is refused in a sentence. A Viewer must not be able to write a report file.

sections.title: Round 1's JavaScript-driven passes, re-clicked
sections.blurb: These were marked passed in round 1 on evidence obtained by dispatching clicks in script rather than through the browser's input pipeline. A JS click bypasses hit-testing, so it cannot see an overlay, a disabled state or a z-index trap.

tests.title: Approval matrix: edit a band with real pointer input
tests.intro: Admin → Approvals. The band editor sets the money thresholds that route a request. Round 1 drove it in script.
steps: Admin → Approvals, open a rule and its bands.
Change a band's upper threshold and save.
Reopen it and confirm the new figure stuck.
tests.expect: The band saves and reads back with the new threshold.

tests.title: Approval matrix: an impossible band is refused
tests.intro: approvals.ts:98 answers 422 invalid_band when the thresholds do not make a valid range. This is the app stating its own rule.
steps: Edit a band so its lower bound sits above its upper bound.
Save.
tests.expect: Refused with a sentence explaining the range is wrong. No raw invalid_band on screen.

tests.title: Nobody approves their own request
tests.intro: self_approval is the one rule an approval matrix exists to enforce. Round 2 left a pending ₦25,000 wo_cost approval routed to the Operations Manager.
steps: Raise a spend approval as the Operations Manager on any work order.
Open Approvals and try to approve that same request.
tests.expect: Refused — the approve control is absent or the attempt returns a sentence saying a requester cannot approve their own request.

tests.title: Compliance findings: raise one on the completed audit
tests.intro: The findings flow was passed in round 1 on script-driven evidence and has one finding in the database to show for it.
steps: Compliance → open UAT R1 — ISO 14001 internal audit, Lagos DS-04.
Add a finding with a severity and a due date.
Check it appears in the audit's finding list and in any open-findings count.
tests.expect: The finding saves, shows its severity, and the audit's finding count moves with it.

tests.title: Risk register: raise a risk and watch the score
tests.intro: The register scores likelihood × impact into a band. Round 1's pass never watched the band change.
steps: Risks → new risk.
Set likelihood and impact to give a high score, save.
Edit it down to a low likelihood and check the band moves.
tests.expect: The computed score and its band both change with the inputs, on the card and in the list.

sections.title: Input, sessions and the edges
sections.blurb: Round 1's r1t57-64, none of which has ever been run. These are the checks that catch what feature testing cannot.

tests.title: Dark mode across the main screens
tests.intro: The app carries a dark toggle threaded through every page. Nobody has looked at it.
steps: Turn dark mode on from the topbar.
Walk Dashboard, Assets, an asset detail, Work Orders and Admin.
Look for unreadable text, white panels and charts that kept a light background.
tests.expect: Every screen is legible in dark mode: no black-on-black, no white card islands, badges and charts still readable.

tests.title: The app at phone width
tests.intro: The field role is the one most likely to be on a phone, and the one nobody has tested on one.
steps: Emulate a 375×812 viewport.
Open Dashboard, Work Orders, a work order and Scan.
Check the nav is reachable and nothing overflows the screen horizontally.
tests.expect: Content fits the width, the sidebar collapses to something reachable, and no page scrolls sideways.

tests.title: Keyboard only: reach and use the primary action
tests.intro: Tab order and visible focus, on the busiest list in the app.
steps: On Assets, tab from the top of the page.
Watch for a visible focus ring at each stop.
Reach the primary button and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>Space</kbd>.
tests.expect: Focus is visible at every stop, order follows the page, and the button fires from the keyboard.

tests.title: Double-submit a create form
tests.intro: The classic duplicate: an impatient second click before the first request answers.
steps: Open a create form (a risk or a work order).
Fill it and click Save twice in quick succession.
Check the list.
tests.expect: One record, not two — the button disables or the second submit is swallowed.

tests.title: Search, filter and sort agree with each other
tests.intro: Three controls over one list is where counts and rows stop matching.
steps: On Assets, search for a term matching one asset.
Apply a status filter alongside it.
Sort by a column and check the row count and any 'showing N' figure still agree.
tests.expect: The rows shown match the filters, and every count on the page agrees with the rows.

tests.title: Back button after sign-out
tests.intro: The cheapest data leak there is: a cached page rendering after the session is gone.
steps: Sign in, open Assets, sign out.
Press the browser Back button.
Read what renders.
tests.expect: The sign-in screen, or a redirect to it. No asset data behind a dead session.

tests.title: CSV import: the template and the picker
tests.intro: r1t50. The import modal takes a file through a native picker, which this session cannot open. The template download in the same modal can be checked, and its headers are what an importer has to match.
steps: Assets → Import CSV.
Download the template.
Check its header row against what the importer expects.
tests.expect: The template downloads and its headers are the ones the parser reads.

sections.title: Regressions on the round-2 fixes
sections.blurb: Four fixes from round 2 that a later change could plausibly undo, re-checked from the screen.

tests.title: The Viewer still cannot read the audit log
tests.intro: Round 2's F4: *:read no longer satisfies audit:read. The Viewer reaching the Admin audit tab was the symptom.
steps: Sign in as the Viewer.
Type /admin into the address bar directly — do not just check the nav.
Look for an audit or activity log tab.
tests.expect: No audit log. Bounced to the dashboard, or the tab is absent.

tests.title: Depreciation preview still computes
tests.intro: Round 2's F10: a non-existent commission_date column made every basis lookup 500.
steps: Depreciation → preview a schedule on an asset.
Read the first year's charge.
tests.expect: A schedule preview with figures, not internal_error.

tests.title: Health score still agrees with its own breakdown
tests.intro: Round 2's late find: the asset PATCH route ran a legacy decay engine, so any edit rewrote the score while the breakdown beneath it stayed on the five-signal engine.
steps: Open NGML-MTR-0042 and note the health score and its breakdown.
Edit the asset — change any field — and save.
Read the score and breakdown again.
tests.expect: The score is unchanged by an unrelated edit and still reconciles with the five signals listed beneath it.

tests.title: No raw error codes anywhere the run touched
tests.intro: Round 2 replaced the displayed error at 113 call sites across 25 files. This is a standing check across every refusal this round provokes rather than a separate click-through.
steps: Across every refusal triggered in this round, read the text on screen.
Watch the console for anything thrown behind a clean-looking page.
tests.expect: Every refusal reads as a sentence. No snake_case code shown to a user.
